accepted.question_text: For every finite set P_n of n points in the plane, does there exist a pair of points p and q in P_n such that every circle containing both p and q contains at least n/4 up to an additive constant c elements of P_n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 Any set Pn of n points on the plane contains two elements such that any circle containing them contains at least n 4 ± c elements of Pn.

accepted.question_text: Is it true that every set P_n of n points in general position in the plane has a convex decomposition of conv(P_n) into at most n+1 convex polygons, where the polygons have disjoint interiors, their union is conv(P_n), and no polygon contains a point of P_n in its interior?

evidence.quote: No element of F contains an element of Pn in its interior.
Conjecture 2 Any set Pn of n in general position has a convex decomposition with at most n + 1 elements.
Our conjecture was proved false in 2001 by O.Aichholzer and H.Krasser [2].

accepted.question_text: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, must there exist a simple alternating path using at least on the order of log n input segments, where a simple alternating path is a nonintersecting polygonal chain that alternates between input segments from F and connecting segments, and the connecting segments are not allowed to intersect any other segment of F?

evidence.quote: A simple alternating path of F is a non intersecting polygonal chain
Conjecture 3 Any set F= {l1, . . . , ln} of n disjoint line segments has a simple alternating path with at least O(ln n) elements.

accepted.question_text: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, what is the largest guaranteed size of a subset F' of F that admits a simple alternating path when the connecting segments are allowed to intersect input segments outside F'? In particular, can every such family contain a subset of size on the order of sqrt(n) with this property?

evidence.quote: Given a a family F of n disjoint closed line segments, find a subset of it that admits a simple alternating path.
This bound, however, seems to be far from optimal. We believe that the correct value is O(n 1 2 ).

accepted.question_text: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed convex sets in the plane, is there an element C in F and a straight line l such that l separates C from at least floor(n/3) up to an additive constant c other elements of F, where separating two convex sets means they lie in opposite open half-planes determined by l?

evidence.quote: we say that a line l separates them if the convex sets are such that one is contained in each of the open half-planes defined by l.
Conjecture 4 Any family F of n disjoint closed convex sets has an element that can be separated with a single line from at least b n 3 c ± c elements of F.

accepted.question_text: Is every simple polygon with n vertices illuminable by at most ceil(3n/5)-1 vertex pi-floodlights, with at most one floodlight placed at any vertex, where a vertex pi-floodlight is a light source located at a polygon vertex that illuminates an angular wedge of width pi?

evidence.quote: The following old conjecture of mine was believed to be true up to December, 2001, when I found a counterexample:
Conjecture 5 Any simple polygon with n vertices can be illuminated with d 3n 5 e − 1 vertex π-floodlights.

accepted.question_text: What is the tight worst-case number of vertex pi-floodlights needed to illuminate every simple polygon with n vertices under the same one-floodlight-per-vertex model; specifically, is the correct bound 5(n-1)/8 up to an additive constant c?

evidence.quote: It is tempting to conjecture that the correct bound for the previous conjecture is 5(n−1) 8 ± c.

accepted.question_text: For every polygon with n vertices and h holes, can the entire polygon be illuminated by at most floor((n+h)/3) vertex guards, where a vertex guard is placed at a polygon vertex and can illuminate in all directions from that point?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 Any polygon with n vertices and h holes can be illuminated with b n+h 3 c vertex guards.
In this case, the guards can illuminate all around themselves.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a threshold n0 such that every polygon P with n >= n0 vertices has a subset of at most floor(n/4) edges whose visibility covers all points of P, meaning every point of P is visible from at least one selected edge?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7 There is an n0 such that any polygon P with n ≥ n0 vertices can be illuminated with b n 4 c edge guards.
any point in P is visible from one of these edges.
